thread:
raja: Heads-up — started initial bring-up of sierra-13b (v1) this morning. Did a quick int4 pass using the usual quant pipeline and hit OOMs when we enable batching >2. Also seeing a small but reproducible quality drop vs fp16 on summarization evals.

toni: Can you paste the exact config you used for quant + batch?

raja: Sure — baseline command: `./deploy --model sierra-13b --quant int4 --batch-size 4 --max_new_tokens 256 --prefetch on`

mira: OOM stack traces? GPU mem frag or allocator fail?

raja: Logs: ```
2026-03-20T09:12:34Z kernel: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-20T09:12:34Z runtime: allocation failed when allocating kv cache 1.2GB
```

raja: Observations: batch-size 2 stable, 3 triggers intermittent OOM, 4 always OOM. If I drop `max_new_tokens` to 128 batch 4 sometimes works but quality for long summaries gets worse.

kevin: Two hypotheses: (1) quantized weights + KV cache alignment causing fragmentation; (2) our prefetch window pulls tensors early and increases peak live set. Have you tried disabling prefetch?

raja: Disabling prefetch and setting `--batch-size 3 --max_new_tokens 200` reduces OOMs but latency jumps. Also saw slightly worse ROUGE on our internal summaries: fp16: ROUGE-L 42.3, int4 (prefetch off): 40.8.

toni: For quality: which quant recipe? Per-channel or per-tensor? We saw different behaviors with approx per-channel recalibration for Sierra family. Also did you run the bias/scale roundtrip fine-tune?

raja: Used per-tensor symmetric quant + 128-sample calibration from the glance corpus (same as baseline onboarding). No extra fine-tune.

mira: For fragmentation, try two small adjustments: (A) align KV cache pages to 256MB boundaries (we changed this on other 13b models) and (B) enable slot compaction GC in the runtime (`runtime.compact_on_alloc=true`). That lowered peak by ~700MB in previous runs.

infra-bot: NOTE: Node g-p100-14 reported high GPU mem fragmentation (>78%) at 09:13 UTC. Collector snapshot id: snap-20260320-0913.

toni: Also test prefix caching off for the canary — prefix caching keeps KV around and can push peaks over threshold for int4 variants. Try `--kv-prefetch none` and `--cache-prefix false` and run microbench with stepper payloads.

raja: Will run microbench matrix today. Plan: batch ∈ {1,2,3,4}, max_new_tokens ∈ {128,192,256}, prefetch ∈ {on,off}, kv_prefetch ∈ {none,auto}. Will post results.

kevin: For the quality regression, schedule an eval run that compares int4 vs fp16 on our 200 long-summary prompt set and save token-level diffs. If degradation concentrated on numeric precision or length truncation that's one thing, otherwise consider small FP32 fallback for cross-attention weights.

raja: Quick results from morning microbench (single node g-p100-14):
- batch=2, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=on -> OOM
- batch=2, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=off -> stable, p95 latency 420ms, ROUGE-L 40.8
- batch=3, max_new_tokens=192, prefetch=off -> intermittent OOMs (~1/8 runs)
- batch=1, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=on -> stable, p95 240ms, ROUGE-L 41.9

mira: Interesting that batch=1 prefetch on is stable. That suggests prefetch increases resident set but batching multiplies live kv-slices. Might be a fragmentation threshold. Try enabling `runtime.kv_evict_threshold=0.65` to evict cold prefixes earlier.

toni: If eviction helps, we can bump default max_new_tokens for Sierra to 192 for hosted tier and provide a tuned dedicated config for reserved capacity. But we need to ensure quality delta <1.0 ROUGE-L point.

evals-bot: EVAL RUN COMPLETE: comparison int4 vs fp16 on 200 prompt suite. Metrics: fp16 ROUGE-L mean 42.3, int4 (best stable config: batch=1, prefetch=on) ROUGE-L mean 41.7 (delta -0.6). Latency: fp16 p95 260ms, int4 p95 240ms. See artifact: https://evals.redwood/snapshots/7345678901-int4-vs-fp16

kevin: Delta -0.6 is within acceptable threshold if we can fix OOMs at batch>=2. Explore mixed-precision approach: keep attention parameters in fp16 and quantize feed-forward weights. That often preserves generation fidelity and reduces KV size pressure.

raja: Ran a quick hybrid quant experiment: quantize `ffn` layers only -> batch=2, prefetch=on is stable and ROUGE-L 42.0, p95 300ms. Memory peak reduced ~400MB vs full int4.

mira: Good. For rollout plan: 1) adopt hybrid-quant default for hosted sierra-13b; 2) tune `max_new_tokens` default to 192; 3) set runtime flags `compact_on_alloc=true`, `kv_evict_threshold=0.65`. 4) For dedicated plans provide explicit binpacking to avoid nodes with high fragment metrics.

toni: Also add a canary ticket for A/B quality monitors (user-visible summarization cohort) and add a regression alert at delta >1.0 ROUGE-L.

raja: I'll implement the hybrid quant artifact and push canary config today. Will update a follow-up thread with perf artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: Nice work. Ping me if you need infra capacity to repro at scale.
